factors.name: aapl_intraday_range_smooth_10d
factors.hypothesis: AAPL_volatility_10d is built from close-to-close returns, which are noisy and can be dominated by a single gap day; a 10-day mean of the high-low range uses intraday information instead, so it should be less redundant with the return-based volatility factors and carry a different volatility signal in years such as 2024 when the close-to-close measure failed.

factors.name: msft_cum_return_10d
factors.hypothesis: MSFT_return_1d is a single noisy day that helped in some years and not others; a 10-day MSFT return captures a slower peer trend that may lead Apple's next move and is less similar to the existing 1-day and 5-day MSFT returns.

factors.name: qqq_volume_to_ma20
factors.hypothesis: Abnormal volume in the broad tech index signals market-wide participation or stress, which is a market state not represented by any existing factor; it uses QQQ volume rather than Apple volume.

factors.name: aapl_intraday_return
factors.hypothesis: The same-day return from open to close captures intraday buying or selling pressure, which is distinct from the overnight gap that was tested and rejected in round 2.

factors.name: aapl_rel_qqq_cum_10d
factors.hypothesis: Apple's 10-day performance relative to QQQ measures whether Apple is under- or over-performing the market; combined with the volatility level it may show whether relative weakness in a high-volatility regime tends to reverse.

factors.name: qqq_vol_20d
factors.hypothesis: The 20-day realised volatility of the broad market describes the regime in which a one-day MSFT move carries information, so the pair may show that the peer-lead signal works only in calm markets.
